* Experience with ISO certifications, recerts, audits
* Experience in a welding/fabrication environment
* Experience in an electrical background

### **Preferred Skills:**

* Experience in UL
* Strong understanding of welding processes

* Salary: $150-180K
* Annual bonus plan 15-25% on target bonus

card.description:
**Standard Job Description**
----------------------------

Manages those who apply quality principles in the areas of: design, incoming material, production control, product evaluation, program performance, reliability, inventory control, and/or research and development as they apply to product or process quality for make and/or buy products. Performs technical evaluations including product requirements, specifications, models/designs, drawings and procedures. Collaborates with program management, engineering, manufacturing, supply chain and customers on quality related issues to ensure quality standards are in place. Engages in product failure investigations, material review board decisions and corrective/preventive action. Ensures corrective measures meet acceptable reliability standards and/or are compliant with requirements. Develops strategies and systems designed to improve internal and/or supplier performance and productivity. Evaluates quality systems for deficiency identification and correction. Designs and analyzes inspection and testing processes, mechanisms and equipment; conducts product quality tests, performs statistical analysis to assess products or materials that do not meet required standards and specifications. Engages in supplier selection process and maintain certification programs.

**Basic Qualifications**
------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college
* 10 years of leadership experience
* 8 years flightline/flight test operations experience
* Quality experience - either in a quality organization or with significant exposure to quality processes
* Ability to travel

**Desired Skills**
------------------

* Prior leadership experience in a unionized workforce environment
* AS9100/9110 experience
* Ability to interpret military service guidance
* Understanding of DCMAI 8210.1 (all revisions)
* Demonstrated ability to work in a blended environment with contractor & gov’t personnel - both military and civilian
* Experience developing BOE through negotiation and contract award
* Interpersonal skills required to develop effective working relationships
* Excellent presentation skills/ability to effectively communicate at all levels of the organization

Full-Time Salary Range: $178500.00 - $331500.00

card.title: Senior Director, Architecture & Quality – Connectivity Firmware
card.description:
**About Marvell**

Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.

**Your Team, Your Impact**

Marvell's Connectivity firmware organization delivers firmware for our connectivity and optics product lines. This role owns the full Architecture & Quality function for that portfolio. Architecture and quality operate as one integrated group, a shared resource to every firmware team and not a gate in front of them. 
 
You will set the technical architecture direction for the portfolio and hold the quality bar across it, treating the two as a single end-to-end responsibility. Architecture shapes what can be verified, and quality is how we prove it, from requirements through release and into the field. You will be accountable for how architecture decisions are made, how firmware is verified and released, and how well the firmware, hardware and systems teams work together. You will lead a global team of senior technical leaders and are expected to build depth in a function that is currently concentrated in a few people.

**What You Can Expect**

This is one function, not two. Architecture decisions set what can be tested, and quality findings feed straight back into architecture. You will own the full lifecycle from requirements and design through verification, release and field support.

**Architecture that is built to be verified**

* Product and systems architecture across the Connectivity firmware portfolio: reference architectures, standards, design reviews and technical decision records, each with testability and observability designed in.
* Product hardware interlink: the architectural contract between hardware and firmware, covering requirements, interface definition, bring-up readiness and silicon-to-firmware feedback loops, with validation criteria agreed up front.
* CMIS and optics architecture: firmware architecture for CMIS-based modules and optics products, including spec compliance, feature roadmap and interoperability, tied directly to conformance and interop test plans.
* Architecture governance that scales: lightweight review processes, clear ownership and reusable components, so teams move faster instead of waiting on reviews.

**Quality as an end-to-end discipline**

* Quality strategy that starts at requirements and architecture review, not at test execution: shift-left practices, requirements quality and design-for-test standards owned jointly with the architects.
* Software Quality Assurance (SQA) strategy and execution: test strategy, automation, regression coverage, release qualification and defect trends.
* Release readiness and quality gates for all firmware releases, with clear exit criteria and a straight, data-backed go/no-go recommendation.
* Quality metrics and reporting to Engineering leadership, Product Management and customer-facing teams.

**Closing the loop**

* Customer-escape and defect analysis that traces root causes back to architecture, interfaces and process, and turns the learning into updated patterns, standards and test coverage.
* A single set of metrics and quality signals shared across architecture, interlink, optics and SQA, so design risk and test findings are managed in one view.

**Organization**

* Lead and develop a global organization (30+).
* Grow and retain senior technical talent, and manage the pipeline, hiring, succession and career paths for architects and quality engineers.
* Build a collaborative partnership with Firmware, Hardware, Systems, Product and Program Management, and with the Optics and telemetry teams.
* Own the function's budget, headcount plan, requisitions and tooling or lab investments.

**Your Team**

You will lead a small team of senior leaders and architects who together cover the function end to end, with architecture and quality responsibilities intentionally overlapping:

* Software quality assurance and release qualification.
* Hardware and firmware interlink.
* Optics and module architecture.
* Product and systems architecture.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Set a multi-year architecture and quality roadmap aligned with product and customer priorities, and drive it across engineering teams that do not report to you.
* Make and communicate hard trade-offs between schedule, scope and quality, and own the release recommendation.
* Raise the architecture bar: consistent patterns, reuse across product lines, and early detection of design risk before it becomes schedule risk.
* Shift quality left: embed test, automation and requirements quality earlier in the lifecycle, and invest in CI/CD, simulation, emulation and lab infrastructure.
* Represent Architecture & Quality in executive reviews and in technical engagements with key customers and standards bodies.
* Keep the function independent and credible: escalate quality risks directly and transparently, including when the news is unwelcome.
* Build the next layer of leadership so the function does not depend on any one person, and set clear delegation across the architecture and SQA leads.
* Manage a distributed team across time zones with clear rituals, ownership and handoffs.

**What We're Looking For**

* BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related field.
* 15+ years in embedded firmware or systems software for semiconductor, networking or optical products, including 8+ years leading managers or senior technical leaders.
* Track record owning both architecture and quality outcomes for shipping firmware products at scale.
* Deep working knowledge of firmware architecture for connectivity or optics products, with direct experience in HW/FW co-design and silicon bring-up.
* Hands-on experience with test strategy and automation, release qualification and quality metrics for complex, customer-deployed products.
* Experience leading globally distributed teams across multiple sites and cultures, including offshore QA/SQA organizations.
* Proven executive communication: able to present risk, trade-offs and recommendations to VP-level and customer audiences.

**Preferred Experience**

* Experience with CMIS and optical module firmware (for example 400G/800G and coherent or pluggable optics), and related industry standards and interoperability programs.
* Familiarity with Ethernet PHY, retimer, DSP or SerDes firmware, and with security features such as MACsec.
* Experience with secure firmware update, recovery and lifecycle practices.
* Background building or transforming an SQA organization, including automation and CI/CD maturity.
* Experience in a matrixed, platform-style organization where architecture is a shared service.

**Expected Base Pay Range (USD)**

218,850 - 327,800, $ per annum

The successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. The expected base pay range for this role may be modified based on market conditions.

This role is eligible to participate in Marvell's bonus and equity plans, including a new hire equity grant and annual equity refreshers, ensuring you are rewarded for your contributions and remain invested in the company's long-term success.

**Additional Compensation and Benefit Elements**

Marvell is committed to providing exceptional, comprehensive benefits that support our employees at every stage - from internship to retirement and through life’s most important moments. Our offerings are built around four key pillars: financial well-being, family support, mental and physical health, and recognition. Highlights include an employee stock purchase plan with a 2-year look back, family support programs to help balance work and home life, robust mental health resources to prioritize emotional well-being, and a recognition and service awards to celebrate contributions and milestones. We look forward to sharing more with you during the interview process.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status.

Any applicant who requires a reasonable accommodation during the selection process should contact Marvell HR Helpdesk at TAOps@marvell.com.

**Interview Integrity**

To support fair and authentic hiring practices, candidates are not permitted to use AI tools (such as transcription apps, real-time answer generators like ChatGPT or Copilot, or automated note-taking bots) during interviews.

These tools must not be used to record, assist with, or enhance responses in any way. Our interviews are designed to evaluate your individual experience, thought process, and communication skills in real time. Use of AI tools without prior instruction from the interviewer will result in disqualification from the hiring process.

**This position may require access to technology and/or software subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). As such, applicants must be eligible to access export-controlled information as defined under applicable law. Marvell may be required to obtain export licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce and/or the U.S. Department of State. Except for U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, or protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), all applicants may be subject to an export license review process prior to employment.**

card.description:
Site: Wentworth-Douglass Hospital

Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. As a not-for-profit, we support patient care, research, teaching, and community service, striving to provide exceptional care. We believe that high-performing teams drive groundbreaking medical discoveries and invite all applicants to join us and experience what it means to be part of Mass General Brigham.

**Job Summary**

The Senior Manager, Quality and Safety is responsible for leading the local execution of Mass General Brigham Community Division strategy, infrastructure, processes, and performance improvement efforts across patient safety, risk management, quality, and clinical compliance. This role oversees and supports the implementation of standardized best practices, safety and quality programs, regulatory readiness activities, and performance improvement initiatives that advance safe, reliable, high-quality care. 
 
The Senior Manager serves as a key local administrative leader and partners closely with system and site leadership, clinical teams, the local ACMO, risk/safety leaders, infection prevention, compliance, legal, data and analytics teams, and other stakeholders to execute both short- and long-term goals for Quality, Patient Safety, Risk Management, and Clinical Compliance programs. 
 
This position is responsible for translating system strategy into local execution while also providing strong bidirectional communication between the site and system teams regarding local risks, emerging trends, operational needs, performance gaps, and improvement opportunities. 
 
Because this is a leadership role in an active change-management environment, the Senior Manager must demonstrate flexibility, sound judgment, collaboration, and openness as the scope and needs of the role continue to evolve over time. 
 
Essential Functions 
 
Quality, Safety, and Risk Strategy Execution 
 

* Execute MGB Community Division strategy for patient safety, risk management, quality, and clinical compliance at the local site, ensuring alignment with standardized system processes, priorities, policies, and performance expectations.

 

* Support the buildout of local safety, quality, risk, and compliance infrastructure, including standardization in training, workflows, governance, reporting structures, and response processes that are in line with MGB.

 

* Collaborate with system and site leadership to execute long- and short-term goals for Quality, Patient Safety, Risk Management, and Clinical Compliance programs.

 

* Provide essential input to MGB leadership regarding strategy, infrastructure, policy development, performance improvement plans, and local operational needs to support high-quality care delivery.

 
Patient Safety and Risk Management 
 

* Execute MGB patient safety plans, including safety event reporting, event analysis, mitigation planning, and follow-up on safety-related concerns.

 

* Implement standardized risk management strategies, policies, and procedures, ensuring that risk management activities align with and strengthen the organization’s approach to patient safety.

 

* Implement and support use of the systemwide safety event reporting system.

 

* Support systemwide and local safety events, including recalls, shortages, and other issues that may impact patient safety.

 

* Partner with site Risk/Safety/PFR leaders and clinical teams to develop prospective solutions and performance improvement actions in response to safety events.

 

* Leads the development and delivery of patient safety and risk management training using culture‑of‑safety data, safety event trends, and systemwide priorities to promote continuous improvement, staff engagement, and safe, reliable care practices across all departments.

 

* Completes, within three (3) months of hire, High Reliability Organization (HRO) training, including Level 3, Fact Gatherer, and Process Facilitator, and integrates HRO principles into oversight of safety event analysis, improvement strategy, and organizational learning.

 
Quality Performance and Improvement 
 

* Serve as the local administrative leader responsible for executing quality performance and improvement programs at the site.

 

* Ensure adherence to MGB standardized processes for quality measurement, prioritized quality goals, quality strategy, and performance improvement activities.

 

* Provide proactive and reactive quality performance improvement planning in partnership with local clinical teams, department leaders, and floor-based teams.

 

* Lead the planning, implementation, and evaluation of process changes and performance improvement activities.

 

* Effectively communicate goals, strategic priorities, accountability expectations, and improvement plans to clinicians and operational leaders, engaging them as partners in achieving quality and safety outcomes.

 

* Serve as the senior local site manager responsible for Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QAPI) planning, documentation, and updates for board quality committee and/or patient care assessment committee needs.

 
Clinical Compliance and Regulatory Readiness 
 

* Serve as the senior local administrative manager responsible for clinical compliance activities, including tracer activity, site preparedness, monitoring, and adherence to standardized compliance processes.

 

* Build and support the local implementation of the MGB clinical compliance program, ensuring standardized processes, staff training, procedures, and governance are in place.

 

* Monitor institutional compliance with Joint Commission standards and other applicable regulations, and advise system leadership regarding areas requiring improvement.

 

* Lead or support proactive and reactive clinical compliance activities, including risk assessments, improvement plans, regulatory interpretation, and implementation of needed process changes.

 

* Serve as the senior clinical compliance manager responsible for management and performance during expected and unexpected regulatory visits, including but not limited to The Joint Commission, DPH, DMH, and CMS.

 

* Oversee submission of required documentation and reports to relevant accrediting and regulatory bodies, including DPH, DMH, TJC, BORIM, and MedSUN, and complete submissions directly when front-line support is not available.

 

* Liaise with system and site teams, clinicians, corporate compliance, and the Office of General Counsel regarding compliance issues, regulatory requirements, site visits, and areas of overlap.

 
Data, Analytics, Reporting, and Dashboards 
 

* Partner with MGB data and analytics teams to ensure reporting to CMS, other regulatory bodies, private payer contracting entities, external benchmarking organizations, and quality/safety reporting programs is timely and accurate.

 

* Understand data provided by system teams and use knowledge of local practices and culture to identify opportunities for improvement, emerging risks, and areas requiring local or system-level attention.

 

* Advise in the development of local and system-level dashboards related to quality performance, clinical compliance, patient safety, and improvement priorities.

 

* Analyze trends and emerging risks, communicate findings to local teams and system leaders, and support improvement planning based on available data.

 

* Prepare reports and presentations as needed for site leadership, system leadership, regulatory bodies, committees, and other stakeholders.

 
Collaboration and Local Leadership 
 

* Partner with the local ACMO and clinical teams to implement system goals, site-level improvements, and accountability processes.

 

* Liaise with infection prevention and control teams to monitor performance, respond to data, and support actions to reduce risk of infections to patients.

 

* Maintain strong organizational relationships and work effectively within a matrixed healthcare environment.

 

* Provide strong bidirectional communication between the system and site, including distribution of pertinent data, analytics, priorities, concerns, and operational feedback.

 

* Ensure recommended improvements are implemented and partner with local leadership to support accountability.

 
Staff Management and Department Operations 
 

* Manage, supervise, and support assigned quality, safety, risk, and/or compliance staff, including recruitment, interviewing, training, orientation, remediation, and performance evaluation.

 

* Establish development plans for staff and support ongoing professional growth, role clarity, and accountability.

 

* Manage departmental operations and budget responsibilities as assigned, including fiscal planning and budgetary recommendations.

 

* Oversee local training and educational programs related to quality, safety, risk, and clinical compliance as needed.

 

* Perform all other duties as assigned and requested.

**Qualifications**

**Education**

Bachelor's Degree Related Field of Study required or Bachelor's Degree Patient Safety Leadership required and Master's Degree Nursing preferred 

 

**Experience**

 

* 3-5 years of safety, risk management, and patient family relations experience required.
* 3-5 years of experience leading process improvement and initiatives and managing teams required.
* Experience working in a large, matrixed healthcare organization preferred.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

 

* Support the build out of safety/risk/PFR infrastructure, ensuring standardization in training, processes, and safety responses that are in line with MGB.
* Executes the MGB safety plans including those around event analysis, safety event reporting/management/mitigation.
* Implement the standardized risk management strategy, policies, and procedures, ensuring that risk management activities both align to and augment our approach to patient safety.
* Implement the system-wide safety event reporting system.
* Support as needed for system wide safety events such as recalls, shortages, and other events that impact safety.
* Understand data provided by the system team and use knowledge of local practices to identify areas of opportunity for improvement of patient safety as well as communicate to the system areas that are at risk.

**Additional Job Details (if applicable)**

**Remote Type**

Hybrid

**Work Location**

789 Central Avenue

**Pay Range**

$99,465.60 - $144,643.20/Annual

**Grade**

8

Our approach to determining base pay is comprehensive, and any offer extended will take into account your skills, relevant experience if applicable, education, certifications and other essential factors. To ensure reasonable accommodation for individuals protected by Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, the Vietnam Veteran’s Readjustment Act of 1974, and Title I of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, applicants who require accommodation in the job application process may contact Human Resources at (857)-282-7642.

**Mass General Brigham Competency Framework**
---------------------------------------------

At Mass General Brigham, our competency framework defines what effective leadership “looks like” by specifying which behaviors are most critical for successful performance at each job level. The framework is comprised of ten competencies (half People-Focused, half Performance-Focused) and are defined by observable and measurable skills and behaviors that contribute to workplace effectiveness and career success. These competencies are used to evaluate performance, make hiring decisions, identify development needs, mobilize employees across our system, and establish a strong talent pipeline.

card.title: Director, AI Quality, Evaluation & Observability Engineering
card.description:
### **Why Patients Need You**

Pfizer's Commercial organization is putting GenAI and AI agents into work that shapes how medicines reach patients, from content creation and review to field and customer engagement. If we can't show that these systems are accurate, safe and behaving as intended, they don't belong in production. You will build the engineering capability that lets Pfizer prove it, before release and every day after.

### **What You Will Achieve**

You will own the evaluation and observability capability for AI solutions across the Commercial portfolio, and you will be accountable for the Commercial AI evaluation and observability standards: the metrics, thresholds and technical criteria that inform production-readiness and ongoing monitoring decisions. You will build shared tooling, datasets and metrics that let product teams measure quality, safety and performance consistently, catch regressions before release, and detect drift and failures in production. You will set your team's priorities and decide where its engineering capacity goes across the portfolio. Success means teams evaluate through your platform by default, release decisions rest on evidence, and production AI issues are caught by monitoring before users or auditors find them.

### **How You Will Achieve It**

* Build and run a shared evaluation platform for GenAI and agentic solutions. It covers offline test suites, regression testing in CI/CD, LLM-as-judge and rubric-based scoring, and structured human review workflows.
* Set the Commercial AI evaluation and observability standards, including metrics for accuracy, groundedness, hallucination, safety, bias, robustness and task success and the minimum monitoring every production AI solution must have. Calibrate automated scoring against expert human judgment and publish the agreement rates.
* Partner with commercial technology leaders to create and govern golden datasets and test sets with domain experts (e.g., medical, legal and regulatory reviewers), including versioning, data lineage and handling of sensitive data.
* Implement production observability for AI systems, including tracing of prompts, retrievals, tool calls and agent steps, plus monitoring of quality, drift, latency, cost and guardrail activity, with alerting and incident response.
* Evaluate technical and model quality, with business outcomes and value measured separately.
* Set the evaluation thresholds and technical production-readiness criteria that feed release gates run by SDLC Standards & Governance, and give a clear pass, conditional or fail assessment against them, so go-live decisions rely on measured results rather than demos.
* Partner with Responsible AI, Legal, Privacy, Cybersecurity and Compliance to turn policy requirements into measurable tests and auditable evidence, including support for AI-related audits and regulatory inquiries.
* Run adversarial and red-team testing (e.g., prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage) with Cybersecurity, and feed the findings back into evaluation suites.
* Evaluate models and vendors objectively when teams select or upgrade foundation models, AI platforms or third-party AI products in partnership with Strategic Partnerships and contracting, so vendor decisions stay joined up.
* Report quality and reliability trends across the AI portfolio to senior Digital and Commercial leadership.
* Set priorities for the AI quality and observability team and allocate its engineering capacity against portfolio needs, based on risk, release timing and business impact. Make the trade-offs visible and escalate when demand exceeds capacity.
* Lead and develop a team of AI quality and observability engineers that will evolve over time, and coach product and vendor teams, including third-party and offshore partners, to own their evaluations using shared tooling.

### **Decision Rights & Escalation**

* **Decides:** Commercial AI evaluation and observability standards, metrics, thresholds and minimum monitoring requirements; the technical readiness assessment for each release; team priorities and capacity allocation; evaluation tooling and platform design within enterprise architecture standards.
* **Informs:** Release go/no-go decisions made through SDLC stage gates and product ownership; model, platform and vendor selection decisions led with Strategic Partnerships and contracting.
* **Escalates to the Commercial AI Portfolio Lead when:** a team wants to release a solution that does not meet agreed thresholds (risk acceptance); a production issue creates patient-safety, compliance or reputational exposure; demand for evaluation support exceeds team capacity across priority programs; or Responsible AI, Legal or Cybersecurity cannot agree on how a requirement becomes a test.

### **Qualifications**

**Must-Have**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering or a related field.
* 8+ years of experience in software, ML or data engineering, including 3+ years building evaluation, testing or monitoring for ML or GenAI systems in production.
* Hands-on experience designing LLM evaluations, including rubric and LLM-as-judge methods, human evaluation design, and statistically sound comparison of model or prompt versions.
* Experience instrumenting production systems for observability (tracing, metrics, logging, alerting) and running incident response.
* Strong Python skills and experience integrating automated testing into CI/CD pipelines.
* Experience leading engineering teams and influencing product teams across a matrix without direct authority.
* Ability to explain evaluation results and their limits plainly to non-technical leaders.

**Nice-to-Have**

* Master's degree or PhD in a quantitative field.
* Experience with LLM evaluation and observability tooling (e.g., OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, Arize, Weights & Biases, MLflow, Ragas, Promptfoo).
* Experience evaluating RAG systems and multi-step AI agents, including tool use and MCP-based integrations.
* Familiarity with AI risk and regulatory frameworks (e.g., NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001).
* Experience with AI red-teaming or adversarial testing.
* Pharmaceutical or life sciences experience, ideally with Commercial, promotional review, medical or other regulated content.

Candidate demonstrates a breadth of diverse leadership experiences and capabilities including: the ability to influence and collaborate with peers, develop and coach others, oversee and guide the work of other colleagues to achieve meaningful outcomes and create business impact.

**Other Job Details:**

* Last Date to Apply for Job: **December 7, 2026.**
* Ability to travel based on business needs
* This position is hybrid and requires working onsite 2 to 3 days per week

 
The annual base salary for this position ranges from $189,200.00 to $315,400.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 22.5% of the base salary and eligibility to participate in our share based long term incentive program. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits | (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. The United States salary range provided does not apply to Tampa, FL or any location outside of the United States. 
This role is posted in multiple locations. If you are applying for the role in an secondary job posting location where pay transparency regulations apply, your Talent Advisor will share the local pay information with you during the first interview.

Relocation assistance may be available based on business needs and/or eligibility.

**Sunshine Act**

Pfizer also complies with all applicable national, state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment as well as work authorization and employment eligibility verification requirements of the Immigration and Nationality Act and IRCA. ### **Why Patients Need You**

Pfizer's Commercial organization is putting GenAI and AI agents into work that shapes how medicines reach patients, from content creation and review to field and customer engagement. If we can't show that these systems are accurate, safe and behaving as intended, they don't belong in production. You will build the engineering capability that lets Pfizer prove it, before release and every day after.

### **What You Will Achieve**

You will own the evaluation and observability capability for AI solutions across the Commercial portfolio, and you will be accountable for the Commercial AI evaluation and observability standards: the metrics, thresholds and technical criteria that inform production-readiness and ongoing monitoring decisions. You will build shared tooling, datasets and metrics that let product teams measure quality, safety and performance consistently, catch regressions before release, and detect drift and failures in production. You will set your team's priorities and decide where its engineering capacity goes across the portfolio. Success means teams evaluate through your platform by default, release decisions rest on evidence, and production AI issues are caught by monitoring before users or auditors find them.

### **How You Will Achieve It**

* Build and run a shared evaluation platform for GenAI and agentic solutions. It covers offline test suites, regression testing in CI/CD, LLM-as-judge and rubric-based scoring, and structured human review workflows.
* Set the Commercial AI evaluation and observability standards, including metrics for accuracy, groundedness, hallucination, safety, bias, robustness and task success and the minimum monitoring every production AI solution must have. Calibrate automated scoring against expert human judgment and publish the agreement rates.
* Partner with commercial technology leaders to create and govern golden datasets and test sets with domain experts (e.g., medical, legal and regulatory reviewers), including versioning, data lineage and handling of sensitive data.
* Implement production observability for AI systems, including tracing of prompts, retrievals, tool calls and agent steps, plus monitoring of quality, drift, latency, cost and guardrail activity, with alerting and incident response.
* Evaluate technical and model quality, with business outcomes and value measured separately.
* Set the evaluation thresholds and technical production-readiness criteria that feed release gates run by SDLC Standards & Governance, and give a clear pass, conditional or fail assessment against them, so go-live decisions rely on measured results rather than demos.

* Run adversarial and red-team testing (e.g., prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage) with Cybersecurity, and feed the findings back into evaluation suites.
* Evaluate models and vendors objectively when teams select or upgrade foundation models, AI platforms or third-party AI products in partnership with Strategic Partnerships and contracting, so vendor decisions stay joined up.

card.title: Director of Quality, Risk, and Compliance
card.description:
At Snoqualmie Valley Health, we’re not just in the business of healthcare; we’re in the business of empowering our community to live boldly and live well. Our commitment to excellence and innovation calls for team members who will build trust, obsess over excellence, lead innovation, and deepen connections within our community. We are guided by our core values, and we’re looking for someone who can embody those principles as part of our dynamic and growing team.

Located in a trailblazing, adventure-loving town at the base of the Cascades, Snoqualmie Valley Health is an independent public hospital district serving a vibrant community that thrives on both adventure and connection. This is more than a job—it’s an opportunity to be part of something bigger.

JOB TITLE: Director of Quality, Risk, and Compliance

POSITION SUMMARY: The Director plays a critical role in cultivating a culture of patient safety, continuous improvement, and regulatory excellence to ensure the highest standards of care for the community. This position leads the organization’s quality, risk, and compliance programs, partnering closely with clinical and operational leaders to strengthen performance and drive measurable improvements in patient outcomes.

The Director oversees the development, implementation, and evaluation of key quality initiatives, ensuring strict adherence to regulatory requirements and accreditation standards. This includes identifying trends, prioritizing improvement opportunities, and guiding hospital departments in the execution of effective corrective actions. Serving as a strategic resource, the Director provides expert leadership and consultative support to hospital and medical staff in achieving regulatory success and maintaining organizational compliance across all quality improvement activities.

This role also manages the coordination of certification standards and survey readiness, including the drafting and revision of policies and procedures related to quality, compliance, and risk management. The ideal candidate brings extensive experience in survey preparation and functions as a Subject Matter Expert in quality, championing a strong culture of safety and operational excellence throughout the organization.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

Build Trust: We exhibit integrity, transparency and compassion in every interaction.

* Oversee patient complaints and grievance processes ensuring compliance, documentation, followup, service recovery, and improvement.

* Investigate and address incident reports resolving care issues and recommending prevention strategies.

* Ensure confidentiality of all qualityrelated data and provide accurate reports to the Board of Commissioners and leadership

* Respond to and prepare information for public record requests.

* Develop and direct strategies for Compliance including HIPAA investigations, auditing, the organizational Compliance plan, and serving in the Privacy Officer role.

* Build and maintain strong relationships with stakeholders including patients, families, employees, and regulatory bodies.

* Ability to function under stressful situations maintaining professionalism and compassion during highpressure events.

Obsess Over Excellence: We have high standards and seek continuous improvement.

* Maintain and implement the Districtwide Quality Plan ensuring alignment with regulatory standards and organizational goals.

* Develop and direct strategies for risk management including investigating incidents, training staff, and addressing legal concerns or actions.

* Assist department managers in identifying improvement opportunities aligned with annual District Quality Goals.

* Assist managers in event management review selecting effective corrective actions for safety issues.

* Oversee patient experience processes and metrics ensuring highquality, consistent care

* Serve as a resource for QI initiatives providing leadership, education, and guidance.

Lead Innovation: We lead with creativity, agility and think bold in our approach.

* Lead efforts to educate staff on regulations and best practices fostering a learning culture that adapts to evolving standards.

* Facilitate and chair committees such as the Patient Safety and Quality Metrics SubCommittee, driving innovative safety and performance strategies.

* Develop and direct forwardthinking strategies for compliance, risk management, and quality improvement.

* Integrate patient feedback creatively using surveys and data to shape new approaches to care.

* Managing and developing quality data reporting, both internal and external.

Deepen Connections: We build strong relationships with our patients, their families and partners in the communities we serve.

* Oversee and manage Patient Relations ensuring compassionate, responsive communication.

* Assure the “voice of our customers” is incorporated through patient satisfaction surveys and carerelated data.

* Build and maintain strong relationships with all stakeholders, strengthen trust and collaboration.

* Oversee patient experience processes ensuring patients and families feel heard, respected, and supported.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Required Education: Bachelor’s degree required in Professional clinical discipline, such as, but not limited to, Nursing, Occupational or Physical Therapy, Laboratory preferred.

Preferred Education: Advanced degree desirable in health care administration, quality management, adult learning, or other discipline with emphasis on outcomes assessment and data management.

Specialty Certification Preferred: CPHQ, Certified Professional Healthcare Quality CPHRM, Certified Professional in Healthcare Risk Management LEAN Six Sigma

Required Experience:

* At least 5-years professional healthcare experience

* At least 3-5-years’ experience in quality assurance, quality improvement, or risk management

* Experience managing quality improvement activities such as process improvement, lean methodologies, quality system assessment

* Experience interpreting healthcare regulations and accreditation requirements and designing systems to meet them.

* Experience with customer service and patient relations

* Survey design as well as interpretation and communication of survey results

* Proficiency in data management, statistical methods, and effective communication across all organizational levels

* Preferred experience working for a Public Hospital District/Critical Access Hospital and CMS certified Rural Health Clinic

* Preferred experience with public record requests.

Skills:

* Strong ability to maintain confidentiality, navigate complex situations, and express ideas effectively to groups.

* Experience utilizing EPIC EMR

* Group facilitation skills required

* Strong communication skills both written and verbal.

* Demonstration of strong strategic and change management leadership.

* Demonstrated ability to work with cross functional teams to achieve organizational objectives.

* Ability to effectively interact with patients and families and deescalate stressful situations

* Problem solving and coaching in a team environment

* Computer skills including Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Visio, and on-line database management

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

* Office and clinical settings with potential exposure to patient care areas.

* Flexibility to work extended hours as needed.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

* Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and handle multiple priorities.

* May require occasional travel between facility locations.

OTHER DUTIES: Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

BENEFITS: We believe in taking care of those who take care of our community. We’re proud to offer a comprehensive benefits package that puts your health and well-being first. With our flexible medical plan, you’ll have access to multiple in-network tiers, including top-quality care from Snoqualmie Valley Health, Eastside Health, and First Choice/First Health providers. The best part? Anyone covered under our plan can receive care at SVH at no cost! It's all about giving you the options and support you need to experience life’s great adventures.

* Medical

* Dental

* Vision

* Pharmacy

* Life and AD&D

* Retirement Plan

* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

* Flexible Spending Account (FSA)

* Travel Assistance & ID Theft Protection

* Pet Insurance

* Other Voluntary Benefits

Benefit Eligibility Requirements - Employees regularly scheduled at least 20 hours per week.

Employee Dependents - Your legal spouse or domestic partner; dependent children until age 26.

Waiting Period - 1st of the month from the date of hire.

PLEASE NOTE:

* The flu shot (during flu season) is required for employment, with exemptions available for valid medical or religious reasons.

* Snoqualmie Valley Health is a drug-free workplace. We complete drug screenings as a part of our onboarding process.

card.title: Alkar - Director of Commissioning
card.description:
Description:

**General Summary:**

Directs and oversees all domestic and international commissioning operations and projects for Alkar product lines. Responsible for ensuring the successful execution of equipment installations from delivery coordination through start-up, commissioning, and customer training, with a focus on quality, operational efficiency, customer satisfaction, and profitability. Provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for the Commissioning Department by developing personnel, optimizing resources, and establishing effective processes to support organizational objectives. Leads, evaluates, and develops commissioning staff to ensure high performance, technical excellence, and the efficient execution of commissioning functions across the organization.

**Principal Accountabilities:**

* Lead the Alkar Service, Installation, and Start-Up/Customer Service Technician teams to achieve departmental goals and customer service objectives.
* Develop and manage the Commissioning Department budget, including forecasting, expense monitoring, and cost-control initiatives.
* Partner with Engineering to resolve equipment reliability, maintenance, and design issues, while contributing to the development of equipment operating and service manuals.
* Coordinate with Manufacturing to manage equipment scheduling, prioritization, and readiness for commissioning activities.
* Collaborate with the Installation Manager to build and maintain an effective service and installation workforce, including staffing, hiring, workforce planning, and performance management.
* Direct and support commissioning staff through coaching, evaluations, feedback, and career development initiatives.
* Manage resources and project timelines to establish shipment dates, project schedules, and milestone tracking.
* Oversee feasibility reviews, specification development, cost analysis, design reviews, and equipment performance standards.
* Support Manufacturing and Engineering by coordinating resources to respond to customer service requests and technical support needs.
* Review warranty claims and expedite equipment repairs and service resolutions.
* Establish and maintain standardized commissioning documentation and reporting processes.
* Develop and deliver customer training programs in partnership with cross-functional departments.
* Ensure accurate and complete service documentation and records are maintained.
* Stay informed of customer needs, industry trends, and regulatory requirements.
* Develop, recommend, and implement service programs, policies, and operational procedures.
* Maintain strong vendor relationships and promote collaboration within the commissioning team.
* Monitor departmental productivity and individual employee performance.
* Cross-train installation and service personnel to improve operational flexibility and team effectiveness.
* Perform additional duties and special projects as assigned by the President.

Requirements:

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Required:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Project Management, Business, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* Minimum of 10 years of leadership experience, including supervising and developing cross-functional teams.
* At least 10 years of experience in a manufacturing environment with strong product line knowledge; food processing industry experience preferred.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and continuous improvement skills with a focus on operational efficiency.
* Excellent interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across departments and with external stakeholders.
* Strong technical writing and documentation skills, including the ability to review and interpret Service and Installation reports generated by Alkar technical teams.

**Areas / Teams Supervised:**

* Service
* Installation

**Description of physical working environment:**

* Office Environment: Frequent use of computer and phone while seated at a desk for extended periods.
* Production Areas: Requires extended periods of standing and may involve climbing ladders, stairs, catwalks, and navigating around equipment.
* Field Sites: Work environments vary and may include refrigerated processing rooms, plant rooftops, rough-grade construction sites, and areas containing ammonia refrigeration systems.
* Travel: Domestic and international travel required, up to 25% of the time.

Notice Regarding the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Application Review

**Notice of AI Use in Job Application Review**

As part of our commitment in creating a fair, efficient, and consistent hiring process we may use artificial intelligence (AI) to help our recruiting teams organize, summarize, and analyze information provided by candidates, including resumes, application responses, and other materials submitted during the application process. AI may be used to identify patterns, highlight relevant skills, and experience, and assist in comparing a candidate's qualifications with the requirement of a specific role. These tools are to improve efficiency and consistency while supporting more informed hiring decisions, which will ultimately be made by the hiring team.

card.title: Director, Health Access & Quality Operations
card.description:
The American Diabetes Association (ADA) is committed to expanding access to care, advancing health access, improving quality, and achieving better health outcomes for people living with diabetes, prediabetes, and obesity. The Director, Health Access & Quality Operations provides operational and financial oversight for the Health Access & Quality Department, ensuring effective planning, resource management, project execution, and performance accountability. Working closely with department leadership, Finance, Enterprise Strategy, the Program Management Office (PMO), and other internal stakeholders, this position translates departmental priorities into actionable plans, financial analyses, performance dashboards, and executive-level reporting.

 

The Director brings strong expertise in project and portfolio management, financial planning and analysis, dashboard development, and executive communications. The individual must demonstrate the ability to engage directly with Finance leaders on budgeting, forecasting, revenue and expense projections, financial variances, and resource allocation. Equally important is the ability to synthesize complex financial and operational information into meaningful insights, recommendations, and compelling presentations for executive leadership and Board-level audiences.

 

**Responsibilities** 
***Financial Planning & Analysis***

* Lead annual budget development and ongoing forecasting with Finance, including revenue and expense projections, reforecasts and scenario modeling.
* Prepare monthly budget-to-actual reports, analyze variances and recommend corrective actions.
* Track restricted and unrestricted funding, including grants, sponsorships and contracts, to ensure spending is compliant and aligned with funding requirements.
* Develop cost models, cost-benefit analyses and ROI assessments for new initiatives and investments.

 

***Project & Portfolio Management***

* Oversee the department's project portfolio, aligning priorities, resources, timelines and budgets with strategic goals.
* Develop project plans, timelines, risk logs and status reports, and coordinate cross-functional teams to deliver on scope, schedule and budget.
* Partner with the PMO on governance, intake, prioritization and capacity planning.
* Monitor project budgets and burn rates, flagging risks early and proposing ways to reduce them.

 

***Performance Reporting & Executive Communications***

* Build and maintain executive dashboards and KPI scorecards that combine financial, operational and programmatic data.
* Prepare executive presentations, Board materials and management reports that explain complex information clearly.
* Present financial results, forecasts and project status to senior leadership to support decision-making.
* Show how financial investment connects to program outcomes and measurable impact.

 

***Operations & Process Improvement***

* Translate strategic priorities into operating plans with clear owners, timelines and success measures.
* Manage resource allocation, vendor contracts and spending controls in line with ADA policies.
* Identify inefficiencies and lead process improvements that produce measurable results.
* Serve as a trusted advisor to department leadership on financial, operational and project matters.

 

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Project Management, Operations, or a related field required.
* Formal finance education or training required, demonstrated through a degree, formal coursework, professional certification, or recognized financial management/financial planning and analysis training.
* Formal project management education or training required, demonstrated through a Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) certification, or completion of a recognized project management training program.
* Equivalent combinations of education, professional training, and relevant experience may be considered, provided formal training in both finance and project management is demonstrated.
* Minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in business operations, financial planning and analysis, project or portfolio management, or a related discipline.
* Demonstrated experience managing complex projects, developing project plans, coordinating cross-functional teams, and monitoring deliverables and outcomes.
* Substantial experience working directly with Finance leaders or Finance business partners on annual budgeting, revenue and expense forecasting, budget-to-actual analysis, variance reporting, and financial projections.
* Demonstrated ability to interpret financial statements, analyze financial performance, identify trends and variances, and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
* Experience developing and maintaining executive dashboards, KPI scorecards, financial reports, and performance management tools.
* Demonstrated ability to integrate financial, operational, and programmatic data to communicate organizational performance and measurable impact.
* Experience developing executive-level presentations, Board materials, and management reports that communicate complex information clearly and effectively.
* Demonstrated experience engaging senior executives and presenting financial, operational, and performance information to leadership audiences.
* Experience managing multiple projects, priorities, and stakeholders within a complex, matrixed organization.
* Experience identifying operational inefficiencies and implementing process improvements that produce measurable results.

 

***Preferred Qualifications***

* Advanced project management certification or additional specialized training in portfolio management, program management, or business process improvement.
* Experience in nonprofit, healthcare, public health, or mission-driven organizations.
* Experience managing financial performance across multiple programs, funding sources, grants, or geographic markets.
* Familiarity with financial planning and analysis (FP&A), enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and business intelligence platforms.
* Experience with Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or comparable dashboard and project management platforms.
* Experience supporting executive leadership teams and preparing materials for Boards of Directors, Finance Committees, or other governance bodies.

 

**Why Work Here** 
The American Diabetes Association ® (ADA) offers a rewarding career working for one of the premier voluntary health organizations in the world supporting people living with diabetes and/or obesity. Our employees consistently say that our mission, culture, work-life balance, and total rewards package are what they like most about working at the ADA. benefits and our culture:

* Industry competitive base pay. Base offers are determined by several factors including but not limited to your relevant work experience, education, certifications, location, internal pay equity, etc.
* A culture of recognition including new hire welcome announcements, service anniversary awards, referral bonuses, monthly All Employee Assembly, appreciation awards
* Generous Paid Time Off, including holidays, vacation days, personal days and sick days
* Comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA), disability & life insurance, pet insurance, and retirement savings
* Guided by our mission, we provide full diabetes supply coverage through our medical benefits program
* A company focus on offering mental health programs and work/life balance with most of our employees working remote
* Joining our dedicated team affords the gratification of knowing beyond a doubt that you will impact the lives and well-being of millions

 

**About the Organization** 
The American Diabetes Association ® (ADA) is the nation’s leading voluntary health organization fighting to end diabetes and helping people living with diabetes thrive. Since 1940, we have driven discovery and research to prevent, manage, treat, and ultimately cure diabetes. We advocate for policy changes and improved access to quality care for all people living with diabetes and/or obesity. Through the Obesity Association, a division of the ADA, we are also working to reduce the prevalence of obesity—a leading risk factor for type 2 diabetes.

card.description:
Division Department: Therapeutics | Quality

Position Title: Director of Quality (Head of Quality)

Reports To: Corporate Head of Quality (proposed; final reporting structure to be confirmed)

Salary - $225-250,000 based on experience

**PharmaLogic is expanding our therapeutics business line. Our therapeutics business, Agilera, is the** **world’s only cGMP-compliant CDMO currently manufacturing and distributing commercial radiopharmaceutical therapeutics across more than 30 countries. In this role,** **you will have the opportunity to work as part of a unique environment that is involved in the entire value chain, from the preclinical phase to the commercial production and distribution of radiopharmaceuticals.**

**Role Summary:**

The Director of Quality serves as the Head of Quality for PharmaLogic’s newly acquired therapeutics business, leading the quality organization and establishing the systems, capabilities, and culture needed for reliable GMP manufacturing. This leader is accountable for the pharmaceutical quality system and Quality oversight of sterile therapeutic drug manufacturing, testing, and release under applicable 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211 requirements. As a member of the site leadership team, the Director partners with Operations, Technical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, and corporate Quality to support clinical supply, technology transfer, commercialization, and growth. The role requires independent judgment, visible leadership on the manufacturing floor, and the ability to translate quality requirements into practical execution while protecting patient safety and product quality.

**Job Responsibilities and Duties:**

**Quality Leadership and Governance**

Lead the Quality function, including Quality Assurance and oversight of Quality Control and microbiology activities within the assigned organizational scope. Set strategy, staffing, budgets, objectives, and development plans; build a capable team with clear accountability.

Maintain the Quality unit’s independent authority to approve or reject materials and drug products, including outsourced products; approve quality-impacting procedures and specifications; and ensure documented responsibilities and appropriate escalation to corporate Quality and executive leadership.

Own batch disposition through authorized Quality personnel. Ensure production and laboratory records, deviations, and required test results receive appropriate review before release. Place materials or product on hold and stop affected operations when quality or compliance concerns warrant.

**Quality Systems and Sterile Manufacturing**

Establish and continuously improve systems for deviations, investigations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, document control, training, complaints, product quality reviews, and quality risk management. Require scientifically sound root-cause analysis and verification of CAPA effectiveness.

Provide Quality oversight of aseptic processing and contamination control, including cleanrooms, environmental and personnel monitoring, gowning qualification, aseptic process simulations, sterilization, disinfection, and container closure integrity, as applicable.

Oversee laboratory controls, specifications, analytical method validation and transfer, stability programs, and investigations of out-of-specification and out-of-trend results. Ensure complete, accurate, traceable data and effective controls for electronic records and computerized systems.

Approve qualification and validation strategies, protocols, and reports for facilities, utilities, equipment, manufacturing processes, cleaning, and computerized systems. Ensure a documented lifecycle approach and continued process verification.

**Manufacturing Readiness and External Partners**

Lead Quality readiness for new products, technology transfers, process scale-up, and commercial launches. Establish clear acceptance criteria and readiness decisions with Development, Manufacturing, Engineering, and Regulatory Affairs.

Serve as the primary site Quality representative for FDA inspections and customer audits. Lead inspection preparation, responses, and commitments; maintain sustained readiness and timely, effective remediation.

Manage supplier qualification, contract laboratory and manufacturer oversight, audits, and quality agreements. Define responsibilities with CDMO customers and ensure outsourced activities meet agreed quality requirements.

**Acquisition Integration and Regulatory Partnership**

Lead the acquisition Quality integration plan: assess inherited systems and commitments, prioritize gaps by risk, align governance and procedures with corporate standards, and manage changes without disrupting compliant product supply.

Partner with Regulatory Affairs on manufacturing and quality content for filings, change assessments, and regulatory commitments. Lead quality defect assessments and support recalls, field actions, and required notifications with designated functions.

For radiopharmaceutical therapeutics, oversee appropriate controls for isotope and precursor quality, radiochemical testing, time-sensitive manufacturing and disposition, and stability. Partner with Radiation Safety and EHS on safe, compliant execution.

**Quality Performance and Continuous Improvement**

Present quality performance and material risks to site and corporate leadership. Use management reviews and meaningful metrics to improve investigation quality, CAPA effectiveness, release reliability, training, and inspection readiness.

**Job Requirements, Skills and Education:**

**Required Qualifications**

Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, biology, microbiology, pharmacy, engineering, or a related scientific discipline.

Typically, 10 or more years of progressive pharmaceutical Quality experience, including at least 5 years leading teams or major Quality programs in a GMP manufacturing environment.

Demonstrated Quality leadership in sterile injectable manufacturing, with substantial knowledge of aseptic processing, contamination control, laboratory controls, validation, and data integrity.

**Strong working knowledge of 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211, applicable electronic records requirements, and relevant FDA guidance and ICH quality principles.**

Experience leading regulatory inspections, complex investigations, remediation, and batch disposition, with sound scientific judgment and the ability to defend quality decisions.

Experience supporting technology transfer, clinical or commercial manufacturing, and cross-functional delivery of significant quality or operational improvements.

**Preferred Qualifications**

Experience with therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals or radioligand therapies; CDMO operations and pharmaceutical customer partnerships; and commercial launch or preapproval inspection readiness.

Experience integrating an acquisition, building or transforming a quality organization, and implementing electronic quality management systems. Advanced scientific degree or relevant professional certification.

**Leadership and Working Expectations**

A visible, hands-on leader who develops people, communicates clearly, and holds teams accountable. Able to challenge decisions constructively, escalate risks promptly, and make timely decisions under pressure. Regular onsite presence in manufacturing and laboratory areas, compliance with required gowning and safety practices, and availability for critical quality events are expected. Travel requirements will be defined for the role. Essential functions may be performed with reasonable accommodation.

Come join our winning team and begin a fulfilling career with us by applying today. 
 
PharmaLogic is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status, or any other protected class.

**Benefits Include:**

401(k) retirement benefit program

Medical

Dental care

Disability insurance

Employee assistance program

Life insurance

On-site parking

Paid time off

Vision care

Able to challenge decisions constructively, escalate risks promptly, and make timely decisions under pressure. **Director, Quality Assurance Operations**

At Vericel Corporation, we are pioneers in advanced cell therapies for sports medicine and severe burn care, transforming patient lives through cutting-edge regenerative medicine. Our commitment to innovation, patient-centered focus, and scientific excellence drives us to develop groundbreaking treatments including MACI (knee cartilage repair), Epicel and Nexobrid (burn care).

**Position Summary**

The Director of Quality Operations is responsible for the strategic leadership and performance of Quality Assurance Operations, Document Control, and Supplier Quality Management. This role provides oversight of product disposition and release, labeling and documentation controls, deviations, CAPAs, product complaints, supplier quality management, tech transfer activities, controlled documentation, and internal audits. The Director translates business objectives and quality risks into operational strategies, resource plans, and measurable outcomes. This position develops organizational capability through effective leadership, succession planning, and talent development while driving cross-functional collaboration and continuous improvement. The Director exercises independent, risk-based decision-making within delegated authority to ensure compliance, operational excellence, and sustained product quality.

**Schedule:** This position is onsite Monday through Friday at our Burlington office, with one day per week at our Cambridge office.

**Essential Functions:**

**Quality Operations and Department Management**

* Provide strategic oversight and accountability for product disposition and release, deviations, CAPAs, complaints, supplier quality management, documentation controls, labeling review, and internal audit programs and tech transfer activities; ensure activities are executed in compliance with regulatory requirements and business objectives.
* Establish department strategy and annual operating plans aligned with organizational priorities, quality objectives, and risk management principles; determine resource, staffing, and budget requirements to support business growth and compliance commitments.
* Serve as the Quality Operations representative in cross-functional governance, planning, and decision-making forums involving Manufacturing, Regulatory Affairs, Technical Operations, Product Development, and Project Management.
* Make and oversee complex quality decisions within delegated authority using scientific rationale, regulatory requirements, and risk-based assessments; escalate significant compliance or product quality risks with recommended mitigation strategies.
* Develop, implement, and maintain departmental policies, procedures, standards, and governance processes to ensure consistent and effective execution across all areas of responsibility.
* Ensure continuous inspection readiness; lead departmental support for regulatory inspections, customer audits, and internal audits, and ensure timely completion of all commitments and corrective actions.

**Continuous Improvement and Quality Metrics**

* Lead a portfolio of strategic, cross-functional quality improvement initiatives designed to enhance compliance, strengthen quality systems, improve operational efficiency, reduce deviation recurrence, and increase right-first-time performance.
* Establish measurable objectives, success criteria, timelines, and effectiveness metrics for improvement initiatives; monitor progress and ensure sustainable implementation of results.
* Analyze performance trends, quality metrics, audit findings, and CAPA effectiveness data to identify systemic risks, prioritize resources, and drive data-informed decision making.
* Partner with Quality leadership to establish performance indicators and business reviews that ensure accountability and continuous improvement.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Staff Management and Leadership Development**

* Build, lead, and develop a high-performing Quality Operations organization through effective organizational design, workforce planning, talent acquisition, and succession planning.
* Develop leadership capability through coaching, mentoring, performance feedback, and individualized development plans; cultivate future leaders and ensure organizational readiness for key roles.
* Delegate authority and accountability appropriately while maintaining oversight of critical quality and business outcomes.
* Foster a culture of engagement, collaboration, continuous learning, and accountability that supports both employee growth and organizational objectives.
* Provide ongoing coaching and performance management, including recognition, corrective action, and career development guidance as appropriate.

**Performance Management and Accountability**

* Establish and communicate clear goals, priorities, performance expectations, and timelines; hold leaders and employees accountable for achieving results in accordance with company values and quality standards.
* Maintain effective communication through regular leadership meetings, team meetings, one-on-one discussions, and skip-level engagements.
* Address performance concerns promptly through documented coaching, performance improvement planning, and follow-up actions to ensure sustained improvement and accountability.
* Promote transparency, collaboration, and decision-making discipline across the department to support operational effectiveness and employee engagement.

**Qualifications, Education, & Experience:**

**Basic Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree with a minimum of 14 years of experience in a biotech or pharmaceutical regulated industry (minimum of 10 years in Quality/8 years directly related to management of personnel). Prior leadership experience required.
* Master’s degree with a minimum of 12 years of experience in the life sciences regulated industry (minimum of 10 years in Quality/8 years directly related to management of quality personnel). Prior leadership experience required.
* Strong working knowledge of ICH, FDA, ISO, and cGMP regulations.
* Excellent technical writing and presentation skills.
* Strong leadership and personnel development experience
* Excellent communication skills at organization, team, and individual levels.
* Demonstrated experience leading Quality Operations functions within a regulated GMP environment.
* Proven ability to lead regulatory inspections and manage interactions with FDA and other regulatory authorities.
* Experience developing and leading managers and building succession pipelines within a Quality organization.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Medical device, biotechnology, cell and gene therapy, or combination product experience strongly preferred.
* Proficient in Auditing, both internal and vendor.
* Prior International experience.

**Working Conditions & Physical Demands:**

* Ability to lift up to 30 lbs.
* Ability to travel if required.
* Must be able to support holiday coverage.
* Must be able to gown into the CNC areas when required

**Why Vericel?**

* **Mission-Driven Work:** Help bring potentially life-enhancing cell therapies to patients with serious medical conditions.
* **Innovative Products:** Work with a first-in-class therapy backed by clinical success and provider trust.
* **Career Growth:** Be a part of a growing organization with opportunities to expand your impact.
* **Collaborative Culture:** Join a supportive, cross-functional team that values passion, integrity, and excellence.

The actual salary offered will be determined based on factors such as the candidate’s qualifications, experience, and skills. Bonus, incentive pay, equity and benefits may be provided in addition to the base compensation listed above.

card.description:
**Department Information**
--------------------------

The mission of the Colorado Energy Office (CEO) is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and consumer energy costs by advancing clean energy, energy efficiency, and zero emission vehicles to benefit all Coloradans. We do this by developing and implementing highly impactful policies and programs, establishing Colorado as a leading state for climate action. The Colorado Energy Office is a great place to work, with collaborative and talented employees who are passionate about our mission and a hybrid atmosphere. Employees report high satisfaction with their work, their colleagues and manager, and CEO leadership. Join us!

 
 

Reducing greenhouse gas pollution and advancing zero emission vehicles, energy efficiency and clean energy are essential to preserving and protecting Colorado’s way of life. These actions defend the health of our communities and natural environment, provide access to lower cost clean energy resources for rural and urban areas, increase investment and economic growth opportunities, and expand clean energy jobs. As part of our mission we serve the people of Colorado with programs focusing on weatherization, energy efficiency, and electric vehicles and a regulatory and legislative agenda to promote the interests of all Coloradans.

 
 

***We are committed to increasing the diversity of our staff and providing culturally responsive programs and services. Therefore, we encourage responses from people of all backgrounds and abilities.***

**Description of Job**
----------------------

* **This is a hybrid position. Hybrid positions are required to be present at the office location for a minimum of two days per work week during the first 90 days, and minimum one to two days a week after that, or as directed by office leadership.**

CEO’s Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP), helps qualified Coloradans save money, increase comfort, and better their homes and environment through proven energy conservation solutions.These solutions include LED light bulbs, high efficiency furnaces and refrigerators, building shell insulation, and rooftop solar arrays, among others.

 
 

CEO is hiring for a visionary Senior Manager, Weatherization Quality & Technical Services to join the WAP team. You will serve as a strategic leader, bridging advanced building science with organizational excellence. This role is pivotal in shaping how we deliver sustainable energy solutions to diverse communities across Colorado, turning technical compliance into a platform for continuous improvement and innovation.

The WAP network spans all 64 Colorado counties, delivering critical energy efficiency and clean energy solutions to diverse populations through a network of six subgrantee agencies.
